purpose: Steps down higher or fluctuating DC input voltages into an ultra-steady, noise-free fixed voltage rail (such as 3.3V or 5V). Because linear regulators operate as an automatically adjusting transistor divider rather than a high-speed switch, they generate zero electrical switching noise, making them the gold standard for microcontrollers, RF radios, and sensitive analog sensor ADCs.

whenToUse.scenario: Powering 3.3V Wireless Radios & Sensors (ESP8266, NRF24L01, SD Cards)
whenToUse.why: The built-in 3.3V pin on clone Arduino Nanos can only deliver a tiny ~50mA from its USB chip. When an ESP8266 or NRF24L01 bursts transmit power, it draws 250mA, collapsing the Nano's rail. A dedicated AMS1117-3.3V supplies up to 1A with zero sweat.
whenToUse.recommended: AMS1117-3.3V LDO Regulator (with 10µF capacitors on in/out)

whenToUse.scenario: Stepping a 9V Battery or 12V Wall Adapter Down to 5V
whenToUse.why: When powering your project from a 9V block or 12V power adapter. The classic 7805 safely handles up to 35V input and delivers 1.5A of clean 5V DC.
whenToUse.recommended: L7805CV (TO-220 package, add a heatsink for loads > 500mA)

whenToUse.scenario: Clean Power for Analog Sensors, ADCs, Audio & Op-Amps
whenToUse.why: Switch-mode DC-DC converters create high-frequency 100kHz ripple that corrupts sensitive audio and causes analog sensor readings (like thermocouple MAX6675 or ECG AD8232) to jump erratically. Linear regulators deliver pure DC silence.

whenToUse.scenario: Custom Adjustable DC Power Rails (1.25V to 30V)
whenToUse.why: When you need a non-standard voltage (like 4.2V for charging a lithium battery or 6V for digital servos). Two external resistors set the exact desired voltage.

basics.title: Dropout Voltage (Standard vs LDO)
basics.text: Dropout voltage is the minimum headroom voltage difference required between Vin and Vout. A classic 7805 has a 2.0V dropout (needs at least 7.0V in to give 5V out). A Low-Dropout (LDO) regulator like the AMS1117 needs only ~1.1V, and modern CMOS LDOs like MCP1700 need just 0.18V!

basics.title: The Heat Formula: P_diss = (Vin - Vout) * I_load
basics.text: Linear regulators discard excess voltage as pure heat. If you feed 12V into an AMS1117 to get 3.3V at 500mA: Power Wasted = (12V - 3.3V) * 0.5A = 4.35 Watts! The chip will become scalding hot within seconds without a heatsink. For large voltage gaps and high currents, use a DC-DC Buck converter instead.

basics.title: Essential Decoupling Capacitors
basics.text: Linear regulators MUST have capacitors placed close to their Vin and Vout pins (typically 10 µF electrolytic + 0.1 µF ceramic). Without these capacitors, the internal error amplifier feedback loop will self-oscillate into high-frequency screeching and erratic voltage output.

types.name: Fixed Low-Dropout (LDO) Regulator (AMS1117)
types.summary: Modern 3-pin regulator requiring very low headroom. Extremely popular as SMD SOT-223 and breakout boards for 3.3V and 5.0V microcontroller rails.
types.applications: ESP32 boards, Arduino Nano on-board regulator, 3.3V sensor supply rails

types.name: Standard 78xx Series Linear Regulator (7805)
types.summary: Classic through-hole TO-220 workhorse. Indestructible internal thermal overload and short-circuit protection. Delivers up to 1.5A.
types.applications: Bench power supplies, 12V to 5V automotive adapters, robotics logic rails

types.name: Adjustable Linear Regulator (LM317)
types.summary: Outputs any voltage from 1.25V to 37V set by a pair of external resistors or a trimmer potentiometer.
types.applications: Variable bench power supplies, custom battery charging circuits, precision current limiters

types.name: Ultra-Low Quiescent Current LDO (MCP1700 / HT7333)
types.summary: Consumes less than 4 µA of idle current itself. Essential for battery-powered IoT devices sleeping for months on coin cells.
types.applications: Battery IoT sensor nodes, solar-powered environmental beacons, wearable electronics
